items.followUp: How can a supersaturated solution of sugar be prepared?

rubric.why: The solution is heated so that more solute can dissolve.
rubric.description: Heat the solution and dissolve extra solute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for heating a saturated solution or dissolving more solute in a hot solution.

rubric.why: On cooling without disturbance, the excess dissolved solute remains in solution.
rubric.description: Cool the solution slowly and undisturbed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for slow, undisturbed cooling or correctly identifying the resulting solution as supersaturated.

modelAnswer: Heat a saturated solution and dissolve more solute in it.
Cool the solution slowly without disturbing it; the resulting solution is supersaturated.

items.followUp: Define a saturated solution and an unsaturated solution.

rubric.why: A dilute solution has relatively little solute in a given amount of solution or solvent.
rubric.description: State that a dilute solution contains a relatively small amount of solute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct description of a dilute solution.

rubric.why: A concentrated solution has relatively much solute in a given amount of solution or solvent.
rubric.description: State that a concentrated solution contains a relatively large amount of solute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct description of a concentrated solution.

modelAnswer: A dilute solution contains a relatively small amount of solute in a given amount of solvent or solution.
A concentrated solution contains a relatively large amount of solute in a given amount of solvent or solution.

items.followUp: Give two examples of a liquid dissolved in a liquid solution.

rubric.why: Air and natural gas are examples of gas-in-gas mixtures.
rubric.description: Give one valid example of a gas dissolved in a gas.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

rubric.why: A second valid example is required.
rubric.description: Give a second valid example of a gas dissolved in a gas.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second correct example; do not award both marks for repeating the same example.

modelAnswer: Natural gas is another example of a gas-in-gas solution.

rubric.why: Magnesium is used in lightweight alloys and in applications such as flash bulbs and fireworks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct use.

rubric.why: A second distinct use is required.
rubric.description: State a second use of magnesium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second correct use; do not award both marks for repeating the same use.

modelAnswer: Magnesium is used to make light alloys, for example for aircraft construction.
Magnesium is used in flash bulbs and fireworks because it burns with a bright light.

items.followUp: Give one property that makes gold suitable for jewellery.

rubric.why: Platinum has an attractive appearance and can be worked into jewellery.
rubric.description: State an appearance or working property that makes platinum suitable for jewellery.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for lustre, attractive appearance, malleability, or ductility.

rubric.why: Platinum retains its appearance because it resists chemical attack and tarnishing.
rubric.description: State that platinum resists corrosion or tarnishing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for its resistance to corrosion or tarnishing.

modelAnswer: Platinum has an attractive lustre and can be shaped into jewellery.
It is resistant to corrosion and does not tarnish easily.

items.followUp: Write the equation for the reaction of methane with bromine in light.

rubric.why: The first substitution product is chloromethane and hydrogen chloride.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct balanced equation.

rubric.why: Light initiates the substitution reaction of methane with chlorine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the reaction occurs in bright light or sunlight.

modelAnswer: This substitution reaction takes place in bright light.

rubric.why: The carat scale divides gold purity into 24 parts; 24-carat gold is pure gold.
rubric.description: Explain the 24-part meaning of the carat scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that 24-carat gold represents 24 parts gold or pure gold.

rubric.why: 24-carat gold contains no other metal in the stated purity definition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as 100% pure gold.

modelAnswer: The carat scale divides gold into 24 parts.
24-carat gold is pure gold, containing 100% gold.

items.followUp: Describe the structure of the atom according to Rutherford's atomic model.

rubric.why: Rutherford concluded that most of the volume of an atom is empty space.
rubric.description: State that most of the atom is empty space.

rubric.why: The atom has a very small central nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the nucleus is very small and central.

rubric.why: The nucleus contains the atom's positive charge.
rubric.description: State that the nucleus is positively charged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the positive charge being concentrated in the nucleus.

rubric.why: Rutherford concluded that nearly all the atom's mass is concentrated in the nucleus.
rubric.description: State that most of the atom's mass is in the nucleus.

rubric.why: Electrons move around the nucleus in the atomic model.
rubric.description: State that electrons revolve around the nucleus.

modelAnswer: Most of the volume of an atom is empty space.
At the centre of the atom is a very small, dense nucleus.
The nucleus is positively charged and contains nearly all the mass of the atom.
The atom is electrically neutral overall because its positive and negative charges balance.
